about.title: Scotts Valley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Scotts Valley is a small city, but its traffic corridors carry a steady flow of commuters cutting between Santa Cruz and the San Lorenzo Valley. Public records show 16 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with reported crashes clustering on Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. — often along Mt Hermon Road, Scotts Valley Drive, Glenwood Drive, and the SR-17 corridor. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, what happens in the days right after matters. Insurance adjusters move quickly, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memories fade fast. We're a personal injury law practice that handles car accident claims in Scotts Valley and the surrounding area. Our team can evaluate the crash, handle communications with insurers, and pursue your claim on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Under California law you generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Our team can help make sure paperwork gets filed before any deadline closes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Still Pays
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a Mt Hermon Road or SR-17 collision, you can still recover a share of damages. How fault gets divided can significantly affect your outcome, which is why early legal input matters.

items.title: Skip the Recorded Statement
items.desc: You're not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and doing so without guidance can be used to minimize your claim. We can communicate with adjusters on your behalf from day one.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near the Mt Hermon Road and Scotts Valley Drive area — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention documented right away, even if injuries seem minor at first. Photograph the scene, vehicles, and any visible injuries if you're able, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company. Reaching out to us early can help our team start preserving evidence before it disappears.

items.question: Does it cost anything to consult with us?
items.answer: No. We offer free consultations, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery. You don't pay anything out of pocket to find out where you stand.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a road maintained by the city or county?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads, like some sections around Scotts Valley, can carry much shorter notice deadlines — sometimes as little as six months instead of the usual two years. This is one of the biggest reasons to talk to an attorney quickly rather than waiting.

items.question: Will my case definitely result in a settlement?
items.answer: No one can promise a particular outcome. What we can do is evaluate your specific situation and explain your realistic options.
